question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3,000 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage interest = **Rate** × **Time**

⇒ 8% × 6 = 48%

**Simple Interest** = 48% of ₹3,000

⇒ 0.48 × 3,000 = ₹1,440

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,440.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = **₹3,000**

Rate of Interest (R) = **8% per annum**

Time Period (T) = **6 years**

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf33704ab8b889998e0b52abfbf1933a1448e465783eeaa6eb2240c0f09f0811.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (3000 × 8 × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 30 × 8 × 6

⇒ SI = 240 × 6

⇒ SI = **₹1,440**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,440.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount (A)

The total sum returned after the time period including interest. Formula: **A = P + SI** = P(1 + RT/100).

Compound Interest (CI)

Interest calculated on the principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods. Formula: **CI = P[(1 + R/100)T − 1]**.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate how long it will take for an investment to double at a fixed annual rate of interest: **Years to double ≈ 72 ÷ Interest Rate**.
